body:
Note that this will construct the `String` whether or not `found` is true, whereas the previous `ERR_FAIL` macro only constructs when true.

This is likely not a bottleneck, but might be better to enclose this whole section in:
```
if (found) {
...
}
```

You could also do this by only adding the second part `if (!is_editor_hint())`, but I guess you can't use the `TOOLS_ENABLED` define there. :slightly_smiling_face: 

I don't think it matters that much either way.

Personally I haven't been too happy with this second part since it was added. It makes the message quite verbose and it's very often wrong - there are many reasons why a resource may fail loading which aren't necessarily due to not having been imported yet.

For example the importer may just fail loading it, because the importer is buggy, or the file is invalid.

We have over 250 issues where this message is included: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20%22Make%20sure%20resources%20have%20been%20imported%20by%20opening%20the%20project%20in%20the%20editor%20at%20least%20once.%22

I doubt most of those are just a pebkac from the user not having imported the project yet (which is what this hint aims at addressing).

So IMO it's better to outright remove it, and see if we can add this kind of hint in a more accurate way (i.e. only when there is no `.import` file or no file in `.godot/imported` matching the `.import` file).
That makes sense it should be possible to detect more of these cases, and it seems a common error.

I've removed the hint for now.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11117 would be a better solution since there would no longer be situations where resources could accidentally not be imported, but it's nontrivial to implement.
